name: Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini
aliases: Idiopathic Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini

criteria.description: Presence of well-demarcated, hyperpigmented, depressed patches of skin with a 'cliff-drop' border
Skin biopsy showing dermal atrophy with preserved adnexal structures and absence of significant inflammation
Absence of sclerosis or induration differentiating from morphea
Lack of autoimmune serologic markers supporting other connective tissue diseases

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions with confirmatory histopathology and exclusion of morphea
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; differentiation from morphea is critical.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-demarcated depressed hyperpigmented cutaneous plaques with cliff-drop borders
searchTerms: well-defined sunken dark skin patches with sharp edges
depressed hyperpigmented plaques with cliff-like borders
dark skin spots with clear drop-off edges

pathognomonic.symptomName: Asymptomatic localized dermal atrophy without induration
searchTerms: small areas of skin loss without lumps
darkening of skin in affected areas

common.symptomName: Symmetric distribution of lesions on the trunk and proximal limbs
searchTerms: symmetrical rash on torso and upper limbs
evenly distributed lesions on trunk and arms
balanced skin spots on body and limbs

common.symptomName: Absence of pruritus or pain in lesions
searchTerms: skin lesions without itching or pain

common.symptomName: Slow progression of lesion size over months to years
searchTerms: skin spots slowly growing over months or years
slight roughness or smoothness of skin

occasional.symptomName: Slight skin thinning palpable on affected areas
searchTerms: skin feels slightly thinner on affected areas

occasional.symptomName: Minimal hypopigmentation adjacent to hyperpigmented plaques
searchTerms: small areas of lighter skin near dark plaques
minimal loss of pigmentation beside hyperpigmented spots
patchy mild hypopigmentation adjacent to dark lesions
small visible blood vessels within lesions
mild spider veins in affected skin
rare involvement of hands and feet

imaging: Not typically indicated; skin ultrasound may show dermal thinning
other: Histopathology: dermal atrophy with preserved adnexal structures, absence of sclerosis or significant inflammation

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of skin induration and sclerosis
Histopathology showing dermal fibrosis and inflammatory infiltrate
White, atrophic plaques often with epidermal thinning
Histopathology showing epidermal atrophy with homogenization of collagen
Localized areas of slack or pouch-like skin due to loss of elastic tissue
Lesions are soft and may herniate on palpation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive skin induration or sclerosis
Development of systemic symptoms such as arthralgia or Raynaud phenomenon
Presence of ulceration or secondary infection in lesions
references: Atrophoderma of Pasini and Pierini: Clinical and Histopathological Features. Dermatology. 2020.
